standard_prerequisites.name: Cohomological vanishing for the constructed submodule
standard_prerequisites.use: Proof lines 1391-1393: H^1(X, F') = 0 follows from this lemma and the assumption that no nonzero submodule of F injects into Q.

standard_prerequisites.name: The Cohen-Macaulay curve situation
standard_prerequisites.use: Statement line 1372: the lemma is set in this situation; in particular dim_k H^1(X, omega_X) = dim_k H^0(X, O_X) = 1 (used in proof lines 1387-1389).

core_obligations: The submodule F' (proof lines 1383-1387): let F' be the submodule of F generated by the global sections of F and the image of omega_X -> F; since dim_k H^0(X, Q) >= 2 and dim_k H^1(X, omega_X) = dim_k H^0(X, O_X) = 1, the map F' -> Q is not zero and omega_X -> F' is not an isomorphism.
Vanishing (lines 1391-1393): hence H^1(X, F') = 0 by lemma-vanishing and the assumption on F (no nonzero submodule of F maps injectively to Q).

The contradiction (lines 1395-1401): consider 0 -> F' -> F -> Q/Im(F' -> Q) -> 0; if the quotient on the right were nonzero, then H^0(X, F) would be strictly bigger than H^0(X, F') - impossible because F' was generated by all global sections of F, so every global section of F lands in F' and Gamma(F) = Gamma(F'); therefore F' -> Q is surjective.
proof_roadmap: Build F' from global sections and the image of omega_X and show F' -> Q is nonzero.
Get H^1(F') = 0 from the vanishing lemma.
Rule out a nonzero quotient by the equality of global sections forced by the definition of F'.
difficulty_reason: Technical lemma (statement 1371-1381, proof 1383-1401): for omega_X -> F -> Q -> 0 with Q zero-dimensional support, H^0(Q) >= 2 and no submodule of F injecting into Q, the globally generated submodule of F surjects onto Q - the proof constructs F', obtains the vanishing of H^1(F') from the vanishing lemma, and excludes a nonzero quotient through the equality of global sections implied by the definition of F'; the final contradiction is immediate from the definition (recorded in the notes). H2: cohomological argument with a definitional punchline.
